chunks: The residue (of the water drunk by) the doves, and the chicken, there is no problem with it, and the birds (as well).

key_terms.فضل: Residue/leftover — water remaining after an animal has drunk from it; a term central to fiqh discussions on ritual purity
key_terms.لا بأس: There is no problem/harm — a standard juridical formula indicating permissibility in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: Is the leftover water of doves, chickens, and birds ritually pure for wudu in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declared that the leftover water from which doves, chickens, and other birds have drunk is ritually pure and may be used for ablution (wudu). This is a legal ruling within the chapter on wudu from the residue of animals and birds. In early Islamic jurisprudence, a key question was whether the saliva of certain animals rendered leftover water impure; the Imam's ruling here affirms permissibility for domestic and common birds.
